title: Quest
description: A quest (#184), one quest chain (#573): a player-facing name and its steps, each one condition met a number of times, or a choice between ways on, each taken by being somewhere or by an answer in a dialog (#636). The steps follow each other in the file's order, except where a step's choices lead to the steps they name, and the quest ends after a step tagged as its chain's end, which every path must reach (#576). One file per quest, named after its id. Each player's progress is kept in their profile by the quest's id, so an id is never reused or changed once shipped.

emits.description: The event it emits once it's done, or taken on a choice (#575): any id, which can start a side quest waiting on it.

somewhere.description: Being somewhere, met once, which a marker points at: reaching a place, or entering a region piece or an instance.

answered.description: An answer chosen in a dialog (#636), met once: the dialog's id and the answer's, as a file in slices/dialogs/data/ names them.

id.description: Stable, never reused: lowercase words joined by underscores.

name.description: The player-facing name; it may name content with text tags, like ${MONSTER:ombulumo} (#733, TextTags).

path.description: Its path mark (#470, #471): which of the story's two paths it belongs to, none, one or both.

starts_on.description: Makes it a side quest (#473), hidden until the player first reaches the place or enters the region piece or instance named here, written like a reached or entered step without a count, or until a quest emits the event named here (#575) or it changes the world (#707, such as glade_purified). Left out, the quest is open from the start.

standing.description: How finishing it moves the player's standing with a faction (#532): the faction's id, and the change, up when positive and down when negative, held on the standing's scale from -5 to 5.

territory.description: Makes it a territory quest (#638): finishing it hands the instance named here to the faction named here, whoever held it before. Every territory quest keeps to the ground rules in AGENTS.md.

faction.description: The id of the faction it's handed to.

steps.description: The steps, in the order the player goes through them where no choice leads elsewhere.

id.description: Its id within the quest, which choices name to lead to it; needed only there.

condition.description: dominated: a wild monster this player dominated. opened: a treasure chest this player got loot from. reached: a place this player stepped into. entered: a region piece or an instance this player entered. answered: an answer this player chose in a dialog (#636). obtained: one of an item this player obtained (#686), counted one per item, once it's theirs: loot in their missed-loot chest counts when they take it out.

species.description: On a dominated step, the species id it asks for; any species when left out.

target.description: On a dominated step, instead of a species, the quest target it asks for (#625): the one wild monster a region piece's legend marks as `the quest target <id>`, so the step's count is 1.

item.description: On an obtained step, and only there, the id of the item it asks for, as loot tables name it.

place.description: On a reached step, and only there, the id of the place it asks for, as a region piece's legend names it.

piece.description: On an entered step, and only there unless it names an instance, the id of the region piece it asks for: its file name in its instance blueprint's folder.

instance.description: On an entered step, and only there unless it names a piece, the name of the instance blueprint it asks for.

dialog.description: On an answered step, and only there, the id of the dialog it asks for an answer in.

answer.description: On an answered step, and only there, the id of the answer it asks for, one of that dialog's.

count.description: How often the condition is met to finish the step.

choices.description: Instead of a condition, the ways on (#573), two or more, each marked where it's taken or taken by an answer in a dialog (#636): the first one the player takes leads to the step it names.

next.description: The id of the step it leads to.

ends.description: Tags the step as an end of the quest's chain (#573), the quest's own id: once it's done, the quest is finished. Every path through every quest, a linear one included, must reach a step tagged so, which the content check walks (#576).
